@Alice Cappo after running all the tests, the “Firefox sparkle” is the option I think is working best.

It’s simple but smart: it has just the right amount of detail to feel distinctly Firefox without becoming overwhelming. As soon as we add more complexity to the shape or introduce heavier texture, it starts to compete with the main logo instead of supporting it.

For motion, we could explore a transition between the “normal” sparkle and the “Firefox sparkle”, where the normal version is flat/neutral (we can use the "default" sparkle icon), and the Firefox version brings in texture, movement, color, and that curious Firefox attitude.

What do you think?

a couple of notes on these:
* hexagons are a typical 'futuristic' shape
* 3d/2d using gradient is something that is already familiar within the brand, eg. the new Kit illustrations, so it might work for execution
* HMW incorporate a sparkle in a less obvious way in case we want to keep it overly familiar? (see Slack example)

Suggestion:
*  Always on your side

We could tied this with the idea of the glow, creating a path forward, illuminating the way...

Other wording options:
everlasting, lively, transforming

a couple of wordsmithing suggestions:
*  -> going beyond existing conventions. 
* differentiated from  -> Classic Window. (it's more important to differentiate from conventional browsing than private browsing)
